notes: President Navon stated that 61 MKs backed Begin (Likud 48 + NRP 6 + Agudat Yisrael 4 + Tami 3, the parties United Press International names). Davar (14 and 15 July 1981) reports Tami proposing Begin, the Alignment, Shinui and Ratz for Peres, Telem and Tehiya asking for a national unity government without naming anyone, and Hadash supporting no government; one newspaper each.

Mandate given to Begin on 15 July 1981 (Navon's letter is dated 16 July in the State Archives account). UPI's 1981 pages returned 403 to a direct request on 2026-11-05; their quotes are from a search-index extract. The State Archives chapter also returned 403; its quote is from a search-index extract.

conflicts.resolution: Two different acts, not two dates for one act. Two reports of the time (Jewish Telegraphic Agency and United Press International) say Navon asked Begin to form a government on 15 July 1981; the State Archives dates Navon’s letter to Begin 16 July. The request date is probable: the letter itself (State Archives file נ-571/13) and the President’s diary (נ-224/4) have not been seen.

term.inclusionRule: At least two independently authored qualifying chronologies, including one official or academic, plus direct support for the date. The Knesset and MFA histories count separately; the JVL mirror is not another independent source. Formal government succession steps are recorded separately in formation.events.

candidatesPending.why: Both Knesset history and Ministry of Foreign Affairs timeline select the massacre and inquiry. The candidate bundles September 1982 killings with the 1983 report. Knesset history also misdates appointment of the inquiry to November 1982. Split the acts and inspect direct dates before promotion.

candidatesPending.label: Bus 300 affair
candidatesPending.why: Both Knesset history and Ministry of Foreign Affairs timeline select the 1984 bus affair/hijacking. The candidate needs to distinguish the hijacking from the later killing/disclosure acts and verify their direct dates.

candidatesPending.label: Golan Heights Law
candidatesPending.why: Knesset term history selects application of Israeli law to the Golan Heights. The 14 December 1981 plenum records passage, 63 for and 21 against. No second independent qualifying chronology was inspected.

reconciliation.note: Not every member of the coalition is known, and its seats at this date have not been counted; the record does not say how each MK voted, so the vote cannot be matched seat by seat. Which MKs voted which way is unknown. The vote: 60 for, 53 against, abstentions not recorded.
61 member seats = 61 for; 58 against. One of 120 MKs did not vote; identity not recovered.
